Definition: Does the government maintain a digital business register?
Comments: OHADA RCCM online searchable register of companies exists; list companies by name/RCCM.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed. The original OHADA RCCM URL returned an empty/unpopulated search page on fetch and was a weak single source. Corroborated with GUFE-RCA (Guichet Unique de Formalités des Entreprises), the national one-stop business registration body, whose own history page states digitisation began with Bangui (pre-2023), expanded regional antennas in 2024, and reached "full digitalisation" (online pre-registration, e-payment, remote file tracking) only in 2025; World Bank Doing Business confirms GUFE handles RCCM registration but historically with manual steps. This matches "Partially deployed" (4) rather than fully deployed nationwide (5); Value Code 4 confirmed.

Definition: Does the register cover births, deaths and marriages?
Comments: Covers births, deaths, marriages per ID4D; but paper-based. Pre-2013 264 offices.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Changed. UNICEF's CRVS country profile for CAR (accessed 2026) documents separate, currently-in-force legal frameworks for Birth, Marriage and Death registration (Family Code Law No. 97-013, 1997), confirming all three vital-event types fall within the register's legal scope, even though "processing" is explicitly noted as manual/paper-based. The original comment already stated all three event types were covered per ID4D but was scored as "Some" (2); this is inconsistent with the evidence, which supports "All" (3). Note that the register's paper-based nature is a digitisation/Status issue (captured elsewhere), not a Scope issue.

Definition: What proportion of the population does the register cover?
Comments: Birth reg under-5 ~61% 2010 per ID4D/WB; pre-2013 >70% Bangui/rural but post-crisis collapse; use as proxy.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed but re-sourced. World Bank WDI/UNICEF-compiled data (via CEIC) give under-5 birth registration completeness of 44.8% in 2019 (down from 61.0% in 2010), consistent with a 2022 World Bank project appraisal noting national registration "collapsed below 20 percent" in parts of the country with wide urban (78.4%)/rural (51.6%) variation. The 2019 figure (44.8%) still falls in the 20-49% band, so Value Code 2 is confirmed, but the cited year/source should be updated from the 2010 proxy to the 2019 WDI/UNICEF figure — no newer national survey (e.g. MICS7) was found as of this review.

Definition: What proportion of the electorate does the register cover?
Comments: ~79% voting-age population in ANE DB per ID4D (~2M/2.5M).
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed with fresher data. International IDEA's Voter Turnout Database records 2,392,946 registered voters against a voting-age population of 3,178,178 for the December 2025 general election (75.3% coverage), corroborated by ANE's official electoral roll of 2,398,158 voters (AL24 News, Aug 2025) and IFES ElectionGuide. 75.3% falls within the 70-89% band, confirming Value Code 4, though the underlying figure and year should be updated from the 2019 ID4D estimate (~79%) to the 2025 election data.
